summary:
VISUAL QA, ROUND 1: not a pass. 10 blockers (8 ui, 2 backend). The core screens are strong, but the portal scrolls sideways on tablets, the first-run screens are cluttered, and several details fall short of Linear, Stripe or Vercel.

**What I did**
- Built 12 accounts through the real screens with the test gateway: fresh signup, unverified trial, trial, invited member, trial ended, paid, payment due, view only, cancel set, pause set, paused, ended.
- Captured 596 screenshots in light and dark at 1440, 768 and 390, and looked at them as contact sheets plus full-size views of key screens. A separate script checked 360 and 320 widths for sideways scroll only.
- Every capture also ran a script check for sideways scroll, small tap targets, clipped text and console errors.
- For real lock screens and tile badges I ran my own production-mode copies on spare ports with `ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0`, then stopped them. The shared dev servers were never restarted and are all still up.

**What is good**
- Signup step 1, the app picker, the review step, test checkout, the success page, billing home in all 11 phases, invoices, cancel and pause, and the email templates all look polished in both themes.
- The plan banner and lock screen are the same in the Portal, CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse, with correct prices and bundle wording.
- Launcher tiles and the app switcher show the right badges with enforcement on.
- The "billing is off" state is calm and honest.
- No sideways scroll at 390 or 360 on any signup or billing screen. No console errors apart from the expected 401, 422 and 404 responses.

**Why it fails**
- **Tablet overflow:** every portal page scrolls sideways from 640 to about 965 px wide.
- **First run:** the launcher shows an 8 step setup guide that pushes the app tiles below the fold, and on a phone three stacked notice bars take about 40% of the first screen.
- **Layout drift:** the page heading jumps between four left edges across the billing section.
- **Phone polish:** clipped tab and chip rows, text truncated mid-sentence, and many tap targets under the 44 px the spec sets.
- **View only:** apps still present every create and edit control as live.
- **Invited members:** they are asked to verify an email they just proved by clicking the invite link.
- **Proration:** the preview showed $23.19 and $23.20 for the same change within minutes.

**Not checked**
- Real Stripe pages, Google and Microsoft buttons, `/signup/company`, and the seat offer in the invite form.
- Confetti and reduced motion.
- The on-screen message when a view only write is refused. My production-mode CRM copy left "New board" spinning for a paid account too, so I could not judge it.
- Hover and pressed states beyond spot checks. Focus rings were checked on signup, the picker and billing home and are visible.

Everything is in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/visual/` (`shots/`, `sheets/`, `audit-*.json`, `scripts/`). File names are `<screen>--<size>-<theme>.png`.

blockers.title: Portal top bar makes every page scroll sideways on tablets
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx (top bar, nav is `hidden sm:flex`); seen on /, /billing and all its tabs, /welcome, /settings/organization
blockers.detail:
Wrong: between 640 and about 965 px wide the top bar (logo, org switcher, Apps, Billing, Organization, search with the Ctrl K hint, switcher, theme, avatar) is wider than the screen. The whole page scrolls sideways and the notice bars and page background stop short of the header. Measured page width at a 768 viewport: 883 px with a short org name, 965 px with 'Northwind Robotics International Holdings'. It is clean at 900 (short name) and 1000 (long name). At 320 wide it also overflows (347 px); 360 is clean.
Reproduce: sign in, open /billing at 768x1024. See shots/b02-billing-trial--tablet-light.png and shots/c01-billing-paid--tablet-dark.png.
Great looks like: no sideways scroll from 320 to 1440 with a 40 character org name. Move the text nav into the menu until there is room (around 1024), drop the Ctrl K hint first, and cap the org name width.

blockers.title: Launcher setup guide lists 8 steps and pushes the apps below the fold
blockers.where: Portal launcher `/` setup guide (also shown on /settings/organization)
blockers.detail:
Wrong: SPEC 5.7 says 3 to 5 steps. A CRM plus WMS trial shows 8 rows. At 1440x900 the app tiles start at about y=890, so a new customer does not see their apps without scrolling. On a 390 phone the tiles start about 1050 px down.
On phones the guide also truncates text that has room to wrap: the title reads 'Set up Harbor Sup…', and the new billing step reads 'Add a card any time before Dec 7. No charge u…', cutting the promise mid-sentence.
A member who cannot manage billing still gets the 'Pick your plan' step with a 'Pick a plan' button.
Reproduce: shots/b01-launcher-trial--desktop-light.png, shots/b01-launcher-trial--phone-dark.png, shots/m02-launcher-member--phone-dark.png.
Great looks like: 3 to 5 steps visible (next step open, the rest folded behind 'Show all'), app tiles in the first screen on desktop, step text wraps and never ends in an ellipsis, and the plan step is hidden for people who cannot manage billing.

blockers.title: Three stacked notice bars take about 40% of a phone's first screen on first run
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/features/shell/shell-notices.tsx, portal-notice-bar.tsx, packages/ui/src/plan-banner; seen on /welcome and / right after signup
blockers.detail:
Wrong: a brand new account on a 390x844 phone sees Test mode, then 'Free trial. 14 days left' with a 'Pick a plan' button on its own row, then 'Check your email for a 6 digit code' with 'Enter code'. Together they take about 330 px before 'Your apps are ready'. In production the test strip goes away but two stacked bars remain. Asking for a plan in minute one of a 14 day trial, on the welcome screen, also undercuts 'no card needed'.
Reproduce: shots/a32-welcome--phone-dark.png, shots/a33-launcher-unverified--tablet-dark.png.
Great looks like: one notice at a time (verify first), no trial bar on /welcome or during the first session, and on phones the text and button share one row of about 48 px.

blockers.title: Page heading jumps between four left edges across the billing section
blockers.where: /billing/details, /billing/team, /billing/cancel, /billing/invoices/[id] against /billing, /billing/plan, /billing/invoices, /billing/activity
blockers.detail:
Wrong: at 1440 wide the tab bar always starts at x=184. The h1 starts at 184 on Overview, Plan, Invoices and Activity, at 360 on Details, at 340 on Team, and at 380 on Cancel (measured in the DOM). Clicking through the tabs makes the title and content jump sideways.
Reproduce: click Overview, Details, Team in turn. See shots/b10-details--desktop-dark.png and shots/b11-team--desktop-light.png.
Great looks like: one left edge for the eyebrow, title and intro on every billing page, flush with the tabs. Narrow forms can keep a narrow column, but they start at that same edge.

blockers.title: Phone polish in billing: clipped rows, cramped activity text, tap targets under 44 px
blockers.where: Billing tab strip, /billing/activity, billing home cards, test gateway card form, launcher setup guide
blockers.detail:
Wrong:
1. The billing tab strip ends in a cut 'A' (Activity) with no fade or scroll cue. The activity filter chips are cut the same way.
2. Activity rows put 'View invoice' beside the text, so the sentence wraps in a narrow column and breaks mid-word.
3. SPEC 13 says tap targets are at least 44 px. Measured at 390 wide: 'Add' 36 high, invoice PDF icon 36x36, 'See the math', 'Edit', 'Manage' and 'See all invoices' 36 high, 'Back to my apps' 36, change dialog Close 36x36, test card fields 38 high, setup guide buttons ('Pick a plan', 'Invite', 'Skip', 'Open WMS') 28 high, top bar icons 32x32.
Reproduce: shots/c08-activity--phone-light.png, shots/b02-billing-trial--phone-light.png; the full list is under `small` in audit-batchB.json.
Great looks like: edge fade on scroll rows, the link under the text in activity rows on phones, every control 44 px or taller on touch screens.

blockers.title: View only apps still show every create and edit control as live
blockers.where: CRM home (New board, Invite, Import), Pulse (New job at /jobs/new, Log work, Add a job), under the unpaid, paused, trial ended and ended banners
blockers.detail:
Wrong: with the red 'view only' banner showing, the primary write buttons look and act normal. In a paused Pulse org the full 3 step 'New job' form opens and can be filled in. In an unpaid CRM org the invite dialog opens and takes addresses. The person does the work first and is refused at the end. I did not see the refusal message on screen, and the integrator did not either, so its look is unverified.
Reproduce: on a server with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0, open Pulse /jobs/new in a paused org or the CRM home in an unpaid org. See shots/v02-pulse-viewonly-write--desktop-dark.png and shots/v04-crm-viewonly-invite--desktop-light.png.
Great looks like: in view only the main write buttons are disabled, or open one small dialog with 'Your plan is view only right now. Pick a plan in the Portal to make changes.' and the banner's button. No form opens. Add a browser test that proves it.

blockers.title: Sign in and reset screens sit at different heights on phones
blockers.where: Portal auth layout: /login, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /verify-email, /invite/[id]
blockers.detail:
Wrong: at 390x844 the heading starts at about y=132 on /signup, 248 on /login, 320 on /forgot-password and 430 on the 'invite no longer active' screen, because short forms are centered vertically. The fields land where the phone keyboard opens, and moving between sign in and forgot password makes the page jump.
Reproduce: shots/a10-login--phone-dark.png, shots/a12-forgot--phone-dark.png, shots/a16-invite-used--phone-light.png.
Great looks like: on phones every auth screen starts at the same height under the logo, as signup does. Centering only applies on tall desktop screens.

blockers.title: Small polish gaps that a top product would not ship
blockers.where: Billing home card row, plan picker rows, signup password hint, marketing /pricing
blockers.detail:
Fix in one sweep:
1. Billing home shows the same button three times in one row: 'Add a card' in a trial, 'Pick a plan' when ended (banner, Plan card and Payment method card). Keep one primary and make the others quiet links.
2. The picker shows a green 'Your price: $9.60 per user each month' on apps that are switched off. Reword to 'With your bundle discount: ...' or show it only when the app is on.
3. A short password shows 'Use at least 10 characters.' right under a checklist line that already says '10 or more characters'. Show one.
4. On /pricing the same action has four labels: 'Set up your Stak', 'Start free', 'Start my free trial', 'Start free trial'. Use one.
5. The marketing footer headline wraps as 'Sell it. Stock it. Ship' with 'it.' alone on a line at 1440.
6. The full page reveal on /pricing leaves the lower sections blank until scrolled into view. Make sure content shows without scripts and for crawlers.
See shots/b02-billing-trial--desktop-light.png, shots/a20-plan--desktop-light.png, shots/a04-signup-typing--phone-dark.png, shots/w01s-pricing-scrolled--desktop-light.png.

blockers.title: Invited teammates are told to verify an email they just proved
blockers.where: Invite accept flow (/invite/[invitationId]) and the verify email notice in the portal shell
blockers.detail:
Wrong: a person who joins from the emailed invite link lands with email_verified = false (checked in core.user for the member I created). Every portal page then shows 'Check your email for a 6 digit code to verify your address.' with 'Enter code', and a second email with a code is sent. They reached the form through a link sent to that same address, so this is needless friction on a teammate's first minute.
Reproduce: invite someone from /settings/organization, open the link, join, then open /billing or /. See shots/m01-billing-member--desktop-light.png and shots/m02-launcher-member--phone-dark.png.
Great looks like: accepting an invite whose address matches the account marks the email verified, no code email is sent, and no banner shows. Add a test.

blockers.title: Change preview shows $23.19 one time and $23.20 another for the same change
blockers.where: Plan change preview (test gateway proration) shown in the confirm panel on /billing/plan
blockers.detail:
Wrong: adding 1 CRM seat on a plan paid minutes earlier showed 'Due today $23.20, for the 30 days left in this period' in one capture and '$23.19' in two others taken moments apart. The seat price with the bundle discount is $23.20, so $23.19 'for the 30 days left' looks like a mistake and breaks the 'same number to the cent' promise.
Reproduce: on a paid CRM plus WMS plan press plus on seats, then 'Review change', a few times over a few minutes. See shots/c03-change-preview--desktop-dark.png ($23.20), shots/c03-change-preview--phone-light.png and shots/c03v-change-preview-viewport--desktop-light.png ($23.19).
Great looks like: the amount is worked out by whole days, so it matches the 'days left' sentence and does not change within a day. If real Stripe prorates by the second, the words under the amount must say so plainly.

blockers.title: Credit balance is invisible and "Next charge" shows the wrong amount
blockers.detail: After any change that earns credit, billing home keeps saying the full price will be charged to the card, and the credit is shown nowhere. Reproduced on a real test org: paid plan CRM 3 seats, switched monthly to yearly (paid $687.14), then back to monthly. The confirm panel said "You get $800.40 credit on your next bill." Billing home then said "NEXT CHARGE Dec 23, 2026. $87.00 to your Visa ending 3184." and the word credit appears nowhere on the page. At renewal the gateway made invoice TEST-0005 for $0.00 (line "Credit from plan changes = -$87.00"), and billing home still promised $87.00 to the card for the month after, with $713.40 credit left. Same on a second org with $65.59 credit: home said "$98.40 to your Visa". The test gateway holds the number (creditCents on the subscription object) but core.billing_subscriptions has no credit column and the plan view never carries it. Great looks like: the snapshot carries the credit balance and the real upcoming invoice amount (Stripe: customer balance and upcoming invoice). Billing home shows a line such as "Credit: $713.40. It comes off your next bills." and Next charge shows what the card will really be charged ($0.00 here).
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/server/sync.ts and state.ts (snapshot), packages/billing/src/gateway/test.ts and stripe.ts, apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing/page.tsx (Next charge and Cost cards)

blockers.title: Promo code is taken but never shown: checkout, success page and billing home state a first charge that is not what was charged
blockers.detail: On the test checkout I typed TEST10 during a trial. Nothing on the page changed: no "applied" line, no new first charge, and a wrong code (BOGUS) gave no message on blur either. After paying, the success page said "First charge $372.00 on Dec 7, 2026" and billing home said "NEXT CHARGE Dec 7, 2026. $372.00 to your Visa ending 3184." The real invoice TEST-0001 was $334.80 with the line "Promo code TEST10 (10% off) -$37.20". Three screens showed a number that was not real. Great looks like: the code is checked when entered, the page shows "TEST10: 10% off your first charge, -$37.20" and the new first charge, a wrong code says so, and the success page and billing home show the discounted first charge.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/test-gateway/checkout/[sessionId]/page.tsx, apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing/checkout/success/page.tsx, billing home Next charge card

blockers.title: WMS dead end for an owner: "No warehouse yet. Ask an owner or admin" with no button
blockers.detail: Two real paths land the owner on a page with no way forward. (1) Sign up with WMS in the trial, do not set up the warehouse, let the trial end, open the WMS: http://localhost:3020/setup-warehouse shows "No warehouse yet. OPQA G has KitStak WMS, but its warehouse has not been set up yet. Ask an owner or admin of your organization to set it up, then sign in again." The reader is the owner. The page has zero links and zero buttons (checked in the DOM). (2) Add WMS to a trial, then remove it with "Save my apps": same page, same words, and /locked redirects there too. Cause: setupCandidates() drops view only orgs, so the org falls into waitingOn and the page prints the "ask an owner" line. Great looks like: a view only WMS with no warehouse shows the shared lock or plan screen with the real state ("Your free trial ended. Pick a plan to set up your warehouse.") and the buttons "Pick a plan" and "Back to Portal". The "ask an owner or admin" line is only ever shown to people who are not one. Screenshot: docs/billing/.review/opqa/shots/wms-trial-ended-owner-dead-end.png
blockers.where: apps/wms/src/app/setup-warehouse/page.tsx, apps/wms/src/server/tenancy/setup-offers.ts, apps/wms/src/server/tenancy/registry.ts (setupCandidates)

blockers.title: Seats can be lowered under an open invite, the screen contradicts itself, and the invited person hits a wall after an account is made
blockers.detail: Org with 4 paid seats, 3 people, 1 open invite. Billing home says "1 invite is waiting and holds a seat." The picker floor is 3 ("You have 3 people"), so I lowered to 3 with no warning. Billing home then says "Seats: 3 of 3 used. 1 invite is waiting and holds a seat." which cannot both be true. The invited person opens the emailed link, sees the normal join form, types a name and a password, presses Join, and only then gets "The team has no free seat. Ask Sam Rivera to add one." Worse, the database now has a core.user row for that person (email_verified false) with no membership, so a refused join still created an orphan account. Great looks like: open invites count toward the seat floor (or the confirm panel says "This cancels 1 open invite" and cancels it), the invite page checks for a free seat before it shows the form, and no account is created when the join is refused.
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/server/usage.ts (seat floor and limit), packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts, apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/invite/[invitationId]/page.tsx

blockers.title: A refresh loses the person's choices in signup and in the picker
blockers.detail: SPEC 5.6 says closing the tab at any point loses nothing. Three places lose work on a plain refresh. (1) /signup opened from the marketing wizard: name, email and company are prefilled from the link, then the fragment is removed, so a refresh gives three empty fields (checked: values were ["","",""]). (2) /signup/plan: I switched on Pulse, set 7 seats and yearly ($1,893.12), waited 3 seconds, refreshed: back to the link's cart ($58.00, 2 seats, Pulse off). (3) /billing/plan during a trial: an unsaved toggle is gone after refresh. Great looks like: the three identity fields are kept in sessionStorage until the account exists, and every picker change is saved to the signup intent or cart (as the checkout review already promises with "Your cart is saved"), so a refresh or a closed tab shows exactly what the person left.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/features/signup (signup form and plan step), shared PlanPicker in trial and trial_change modes

blockers.title: The warehouse limit and view only are only told after the person fills a long form, and the way back drops their work
blockers.detail: WMS, plan covers 1 warehouse, 1 in use. "Create warehouse" opens the full two step drawer (about 15 required fields) with no word about the plan. Only on the final save does it answer 402 with "This warehouse is not in your plan yet. Your plan covers 1 warehouse. Add one more for $279.20 more per month." The "Add to my plan" button then leaves the WMS in the same tab, so the typed warehouse is gone. After "Confirm change" the flash link "Back to WMS" goes to the WMS root (http://localhost:3000), not to the warehouses page, so the person starts the form again. Same pattern in Projects in view only: the three step New project wizard takes every answer and only the last click says "Your plan is view only right now." Great looks like: the count is known, so clicking "Create warehouse" at the limit shows the price and "Add to my plan" first; the link carries a return path to /settings/warehouses; and in view only the create buttons say so before a form opens.
blockers.where: apps/wms/src/components/facility/warehouses/warehouse-drawer.tsx, apps/wms/src/server/auth/plan.ts (billing link return path), apps/projects new project wizard

blockers.title: A stale confirm panel is not caught when another change landed first
blockers.detail: SPEC 6.3 and 12.4 say a change that landed since the preview must reload the panel with "The amount changed while you were looking." Reproduced with two tabs on one org at 3 seats with $32.80 credit. Tab 1: preview "Add 1 seat. Due today $0.00. Then $131.20 per month." Tab 2: add 2 seats and confirm (now 5 seats, credit used). Tab 1: press Confirm change. It went through with no message and took the plan from 5 seats down to 4, which is a removal, under a panel titled "Add 1 seat". It passed because only the due today amount is compared ($0.00 equals $0.00). Great looks like: the preview carries what it was based on (subscription items and period, or the gateway synced time) and the confirm refuses with the "amount changed" message when the base moved, even if the dollars match.
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/server/changes.ts (preview token and confirm check)

blockers.title: Billing manager row survives when the person is removed from the organization
blockers.detail: Owner made Casey a billing manager, then removed Casey from the organization on /settings/organization. core.member no longer has Casey, but core.billing_managers still has the row (count 1 after removal). Emails are safe because recipients are joined to members, but the role comes back by itself if the person is invited again, which breaks "Only an owner can add or remove a billing manager". I did not run the invite again step; the row left behind is the proven part. Great looks like: removing a member (or the member leaving) deletes their billing_managers row in the same hook, with an activity line.
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts and roles.ts, core.billing_managers

blockers.title: A person who joined from an emailed invite is still asked to verify that same email
blockers.detail: Casey accepted an invite from the link in the invite email. The launcher then shows "Check your email for a 6 digit code to verify your address. Enter code" on every page, and once made a billing manager the plan page says "Verify your email first. It takes one minute." The invite link was sent to that address, so opening it already proved it. Linear, Slack and Notion do not ask twice. Great looks like: accepting an invite with the invited address marks the email verified, so an invited person never sees the code banner.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/invite/[invitationId] accept action, packages/auth invitation accept hook

blockers.title: Setup guide shows 8 or 9 steps, not the 3 to 5 the spec and must have 27 require
blockers.detail: Launcher after signup with CRM and Pulse: "1 of 9 complete. About 13 min left." With CRM and Projects: "0 of 8 complete. About 12 min left." Pulse alone: 6. SPEC 5.7 and must have 27 say 3 to 5 steps tied to the chosen apps. For a first minute in the product, nine numbered steps reads as homework, not as a quick start. Great looks like: at most 5 steps on the launcher (business answers, invite, the first real step of each chosen app up to the cap, pick your plan), with the deeper per app steps kept in each app's own guide.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/features/setup (guide model) and launcher

blockers.title: Console errors on normal paths
blockers.detail: The owner's rule is zero console errors. These show in the browser console during expected, handled cases: signup with an email that already exists (POST /api/auth/sign-up/email 422), wrong password on /login (401), a bad invite email (400), inviting when all seats are used, which is the path that opens the seat offer (POST /api/auth/organization/invite-member 403), and the WMS warehouse limit (POST /api/warehouses 402). Each prints "Failed to load resource". I also saw one React hydration error (minified error 418) on the CRM home in a production build for a plain member of a paid org; it did not come back in two more loads as the owner, so treat it as seen once. Great looks like: expected refusals come back as 200 with an error body from a server action, or are checked before the call (the seat count is already on the page), so the console stays clean; and the CRM home is checked for a text mismatch between server and browser.
blockers.where: apps/portal signup form, login form, settings/organization invite form; apps/wms warehouse drawer; apps/crm home page

blockers.title: Old confirmation message stays on billing home after the state moved on (test tools)
blockers.detail: After "Cancel my plan", then the test tools (skip 30 days, run renewals) and a reload, billing home showed the badge ENDED together with the old flash "Your plan is set to end. You keep everything until then. You can undo this any time before that day." The same happened after a pause: badge PAUSED with "Your pause is set. No bills while paused." A plain reload with no test tool in between clears the flash correctly, so this is tied to the test tool actions refreshing the page with the old notice still in the router's address. It only shows in test mode, but that is where the owner will demo the product, and the two lines contradict each other. Great looks like: a test tool run drops the notice parameter before it refreshes, so the flash never outlives the action it confirmed.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/features/billing/home/flash.tsx and the test tools panel

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. 12 blockers. None is a fake charge or an access leak, but several put a wrong number or a dead end in front of a customer.

How I tested: I drove the real product with Playwright and direct API calls against the shared dev stack, and read core.entitlements, billing_subscriptions, billing_invoices, billing_events, billing_emails and the audit log after each step. I made seven test organizations (names start with "OPQA"); they are still in the local database. I did not edit product code and did not restart the shared servers.

What works well, with real results:
- **Wizard to signup:** the handoff took 383 ms. Name, email and company arrive prefilled, and back and refresh inside the wizard keep its state.
- **Signup form:** bad inputs, a weak password and a duplicate email (with a Sign in link that keeps the cart) all give the right message. Submit to picker took 740 ms.
- **Trial start:** a double click starts one trial. Rows are right: source trial, 14 days out, one billing_trial_uses row.
- **Email code:** wrong code, old code and resend all behave. Skipping never blocks.
- **Checkout:** declined, not enough money, 3DS fail and 3DS approve all behave. A decline writes no rows. A paid, bogus or missing session id never grants anything.
- **Proration:** every preview equalled the invoice to the cent for add seat, remove seat, add Projects, remove WMS, losing the bundle, monthly to yearly and back, and add warehouse ($279.18).
- **Webhooks:** replays answer "duplicate" with one ledger row. Forged "deleted", "paused", "payment_failed" and 40 day old events for a healthy plan changed nothing and sent no email. Bad, old, missing or tampered signatures get 400 and no row. Cross org ids are ignored.
- **Failed payment:** past due with banner and email, one email per retry, the last day email, view only on day 8. A declined replacement card is refused. A good card recovers the plan in 1.3 s with a receipt.
- **Cancel and pause:** cancel with reason, keep, cancel again, ended, and paying again with no second trial all work. Pause, undo pause, paused and start again now all work.
- **Roles:** a member sees only the small card on every billing URL and gets 404 on PDFs and the export. An admin can read but not change. A billing manager can manage.
- **Two orgs for one user:** switching works and invoices are isolated per active organization.
- **Seats and invites:** the seat offer on invite shows the price ($32.80) and charges only after yes.
- **Product apps, checked on private copies with enforcement on:** trial banner, lock screens with price, view only refusal message, and banners for payment due, cancel, pause and ended in CRM and Projects.
- **Phone width:** no sideways scroll at 360 px on 12 screens.
- **Speed:** no step took over 2 seconds.

Not verified:
- Launcher tiles and app switcher badges in the Portal with enforcement on. The shared Portal runs with the allow all switch and I was told not to restart it.
- Real Stripe, real email and social sign in. No keys exist.
- A write attempt while the plan was unpaid. I checked the view only banner in that state, and the write refusal only after trial end.
- The full password reset. I stopped before saving a new password.
- The WMS trial banner with a warehouse set up.

Smaller notes, not counted as blockers:
- An app removed from a trial a minute ago shows the badge "View only" next to "Free during your trial".
- Confirming a pause writes an empty row in billing_cancel_feedback.
- The cancel banner in other apps can lag up to 60 seconds, as designed.

Everything is in /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/opqa/ (gitignored): the scripts, the `out-*.txt` logs and `shots/`.

blockers.title: Two checkout sessions can both be paid: the org ends up with two live subscriptions and is billed twice
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/checkout.ts (createCheckout, applyCheckoutSession), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/sync.ts (applySubscriptionSnapshot), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/gateway/stripe.ts (createCheckoutSession)
blockers.detail: createCheckout only refuses when core.billing_subscriptions already holds a live row. Nothing stops a second session from being opened before the first is paid (two tabs, back button then Pay again, or an owner and a billing manager paying at the same moment), and nothing expires the other open sessions or rejects the second completion. Reproduced with the real code path on the test gateway (/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec1/probe1.mts, run with `cd packages/billing && pnpm exec tsx ../../docs/billing/.review/sec1/probe1.mts`): two createCheckout calls for one org, then completeTestCheckout on both. Result: both payments succeed, two paid invoices ($29.00 and $14,500.00), two gateway subscriptions with status active, and our row tracks only the second one. The first one is orphaned: the UI can never cancel it and it keeps renewing. On Stripe it is worse, because applySubscriptionSnapshot only skips a foreign subscription when it is NOT live, so every renewal event of either subscription overwrites the row and the entitlement seats flip back and forth. Great looks like: (1) createCheckout expires any other open session of the customer before making a new one (Stripe checkout.sessions.expire, same in the test gateway), (2) applyCheckoutSession and the subscription webhook detect a second live subscription for an org that already has a different live one and cancel and refund the newcomer (with an audit row and a log line) instead of overwriting, (3) the test gateway refuses to complete a session when the org already has a live subscription, (4) a database test for 'two sessions, both paid' that asserts one live subscription and one charge.

blockers.title: The browser picks the proration date (up to 1 hour in the past), which mints free account credit on every upgrade and downgrade cycle
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/changes.ts (applyPlanChange, lines 160 to 170 of the function: the prorationDate window), /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/server/billing-actions.ts (confirmPlanChangeAction)
blockers.detail: confirmPlanChangeAction takes prorationDate from the client and applyPlanChange accepts any value from now minus 1 hour to now plus 60 seconds. It is never compared with the time of the last change to the subscription. So a manager can upgrade with an honest date, then one minute later downgrade with a date 59 minutes in the past, and is credited for 59 minutes of the big plan that were never paid for. Reproduced through applyPlanChange on the test gateway, whose proration rule is the same as Stripe's (same probe file as above): CRM monthly, 1 seat to 500 seats and back. Each cycle added 1,943 cents of credit. After 5 cycles the credit balance was 998,567 cents against 988,852 cents ever charged, a net gain of $97.15, and upgrades 2 to 5 were paid entirely from credit with no card charge. The 20 changes per hour limit allows 10 cycles per hour, about $194 of credit per hour for one org, enough to cover a normal bill forever. The Stripe adapter passes the same date straight to subscriptions.update as proration_date, so the live path has the same hole. Great looks like: the server never trusts a client time for money. Either always prorate at server now and only compare the amount with expectedDueTodayCents (tell the person the price changed if it differs by more than the tolerance), or clamp the accepted date to no older than a few minutes AND never earlier than the subscription's last change (updatedAt of the row). Add a test that an upgrade followed by a back dated downgrade leaves credit less than or equal to what was paid.

blockers.title: An account with an unverified email can send invitation emails to any address (the verified email rule for inviting is only in the UI)
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts (beforeCreateInvitation), /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/app/(app)/settings/organization/invite-member-form.tsx (the only place the rule is checked)
blockers.detail: SPEC.md line 297 says a verified email is needed before inviting people. Paying and plan changes enforce this on the server (email_unverified), inviting does not. Reproduced against the running dev portal with curl: POST /api/auth/sign-up/email with a made up address (emailVerified false), POST /api/auth/organization/create with the name 'Big Bank Security', then POST /api/auth/organization/invite-member with organizationId and any recipient. Answer 200, and core.billing_emails got a queued 'invitation' row to the stranger with orgName 'Big Bank Security' and the attacker's chosen inviter name. 29 invites went through in a few seconds before the 30 per 10 minutes per IP limit answered. In production these leave from KitStak's own sending domain, so anyone can use the product to send branded phishing or spam without ever proving an address, and it will hurt mail reputation for receipts and codes. (Probe rows were deleted afterwards.) Great looks like: the rule sits in the shared hook so it holds at every door (Portal, CRM, WMS, Projects, Pulse): beforeCreateInvitation refuses with a plain sentence and code EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED when the inviter's email is not verified, with a decision written down for older CRM users who were never asked to verify. Add a per organization daily cap on invite emails as well as the per IP limit, and a test that calls the endpoint directly.

blockers.title: Microsoft is a trusted provider for automatic account linking with the multi tenant 'common' default, which can allow account takeover by email claim
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/auth/src/create-auth.ts (account.accountLinking.trustedProviders), /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/features/signup/social.ts (tenantId default 'common'), /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/GO-LIVE.md
blockers.detail: Not reproducible here because no Microsoft keys exist, so this is from reading the installed code (better-auth 1.7.21). In dist/oauth2/link-account.mjs a provider listed in trustedProviders is linked to an existing verified local account even when the provider did not confirm the email. The Microsoft provider (microsoft-entra-id.mjs) sets emailVerified false for work accounts that carry no email_verified claim, and the email claim of an Entra tenant is set by that tenant's admin. With tenant 'common', anyone can make their own tenant, set a user's mail to a KitStak customer's address and click Continue with Microsoft: the account is linked and they are signed in as the customer, with their organizations, billing and data. Microsoft drops unverified email claims by default only for app registrations made after June 2023 and only while that setting is left on, and GO-LIVE.md says nothing about it. Google is safe (it always sends email_verified). The local unverified case is already safe (requireLocalEmailVerified defaults to true). Great looks like: Microsoft is not in trustedProviders unless the claim is proven: read the xms_edov optional claim (or verified_primary_email) in mapProfileToUser and only then report emailVerified true, drop 'microsoft' from the trusted list, show a plain 'Sign in with your password, then connect Microsoft in settings' message when linking is refused, and add the Entra app registration steps to GO-LIVE.md. A unit test should cover 'Microsoft profile without a verified email does not link to an existing account'.

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. Four blockers, all backend. Three are reproduced with real commands; the fourth is from reading the installed library, because no Microsoft keys exist.

What I ran
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in packages/billing: 21 files, 408 tests, all pass.
- Forged and unsigned POSTs to the dev portal: `/api/billing/webhooks/test` answers 400 bad_signature and writes no ledger row; `/api/billing/webhooks/stripe` answers 503 with no keys.
- A tampered body with a valid signature answers 400. One event delivered twice at once gives one `processed` and one `duplicate`, with one audit row and one receipt.
- The return page racing the webhook (two concurrent `syncCheckoutSession` calls, three runs) gives one `plan.started` row and one email.
- Auth probes: sign in by code answers 404, sign in errors are the same for known and unknown emails, a reset request for an unknown email answers success, and a foreign Origin answers 403.
- Scratch probes are in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec1/probe1.mts` and `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec1/probe2.mts` (gitignored). Probe data was removed afterwards.

What is solid
- Webhooks verify the signature on the raw body first, and the ledger row commits in the same transaction as the state change.
- Handlers fetch the current object from the gateway and never trust the event body.
- Every price comes from the catalog (integer cents; the four price columns check out by hand). No action accepts an amount to charge.
- The org always comes from the session. Invoice, PDF and CSV routes are scoped to that org, and CSV cells are guarded against formulas.
- The test gateway, its pages and its actions all check the mode. Production with no keys fails closed.
- Return URLs are built on the server, and `safeNextPath` is sound.
- Code attempts are counted (5 per code, 20 sends per day per address).
- Emails escape HTML. No secrets in the diff.
- Migration 0007 is additive and guarded.
- Entitlement caches re-read any answer that is not full access, so a payment shows on the next request in every app.

Not blockers, but worth fixing
- **Test gateway under load:** it reads through the pool while the caller holds a transaction. With 5 deliveries at once and a pool of 4, 3 answered 500. This is test mode only.
- **Promo codes:** `allow_promotion_codes` is on, but `recurringCents` and the "next charge" figure ignore a repeating or forever coupon, so those would show the wrong amount.
- **No rate limit** on `previewPlanChangeAction` (a Stripe call), `openCardUpdateAction` or `updateBillingDetailsAction`.
- **GET that pays:** `/billing?updated=card` pays the open invoice on a GET. It only charges the org's own overdue bill, but a POST would be cleaner.
- **`NODE_ENV` default:** the portal env schema defaults it to `development`, which fails open to test mode if it is ever unset.
- **Plain text codes:** verification and reset codes sit in `core.billing_emails` payload and html.
- **Silent skips:** database tests use `skipIf(!available)`, so a run with no database is green without testing webhooks, sync or trials. The repo has no CI workflow, so nothing guards this.
- **Dead parameter:** `billingOrganizationOptions` takes `allowAll` and never reads it.
- **Trial limit race:** the one trial per person check is not atomic across two orgs started at the same moment.
- **Spec decision, noted only:** signup tells a person that an email already has an account (SPEC line 231).

Not verified: real Stripe behaviour (Checkout, Billing Portal, pending updates on an interval change), Resend, and Google or Microsoft sign in.

Not passed. Head to head score is 20 of 30 with one zero; the bar in COMPETITORS.md section 6 is 24 or more with no zero. Full scorecard: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/reviews/critic-round-1.md. Scripts and screenshots: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/critic1/.

How I tested: real Chromium against the shared dev stack, three fresh signups. Riley on desktop from the site's /pricing ran the whole flow, from signup mistakes through promo, trial end, seat changes, pause, cancel, a failed renewal and an invite at the seat limit. Jo ran signup on a 360 px phone in dark. Sam came through the 5 step wizard and went keyboard only from the password on.

Already better than Stripe, Slack, Linear and the rest:
- The price math in words on every screen, and "See the math".
- The billing page: all five answers on first paint at 1280 by 800, with usage against paid.
- Seat changes: one rule, cost shown before confirm, credit on removal.
- The failed payment banner and email: amount, last 4, retry date, access date.
- Cancel, pause and undo. Best I have used.
- The wizard handoff and the fast path: 4 fields, 5 clicks, account made in under a second.

Why it fails:
- Twice the screen named a charge and the gateway charged a different amount. With promo TEST10 every screen said the first charge was $395.20; the invoice was $355.68. After I removed seats, billing home said the next charge was $372.00; the renewal attempt was $325.61. Both were in my favor, but a billing product cannot show a wrong number. That is the zero on "could a charge surprise me".
- The trial banner's "Pick a plan" opens a page with a greyed out "Save my apps" button.
- Every start button on the home page goes to the 5 step wizard, about 10 screens before the product.
- A wrong email at signup means starting over.
- The password hint names one rule and the form has four.
- The setup guide promises 5 steps, then shows 8, then 12.
- The invoice lists the promo twice and hides the bundle discount.
- There is no refund answer, security line or support contact on the way in.
- Real Stripe has never been run.

Not verified by me:
- Lock screens and view only apps. The shared servers run with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=1 and I was told not to restart them, so I looked at the visual reviewer's captures from the same build.
- Paste into the 6 digit code field. My made up clipboard event did not fill the field, which proves nothing either way.
- The billing manager role as a second person.
- The unpaid (view only after 7 days) state. Pay now cleared the late payment before I got there.

The integrator's 5 failing WMS unit tests are outside signup and billing, so I did not score them.

blockers.title: Promo code accepted but every screen still shows the full first charge
blockers.detail: Repro: trial org with CRM 5 seats and WMS 1 warehouse, monthly. Billing, Add a card, Continue to test checkout, type TEST10. The page confirms '10% off your first charge' but the summary beside it still says 'First charge $395.20 on Dec 7, 2026'. The success page, the billing home Next charge card ('$395.20 to your Visa ending 3184') and the plan banner ('Your first payment of $395.20 is on Dec 7') all say $395.20. After 'Skip to the end of the trial', invoice TEST-0001 charged $355.68. Great: the moment the code is accepted the summary gains a line 'Promo code TEST10 (10% off) -$39.52' and 'First charge $355.68'. Success page, billing home and the banner read the amount from the gateway's upcoming invoice, so the number shown is the number charged. Add an e2e check that the first charge shown equals the first invoice total when a promo is used.
blockers.where: apps/portal test-gateway checkout page, /billing/checkout/success, /billing Next charge card, plan banner text (planNoticeFor in packages/billing), snapshot of upcoming invoice

blockers.title: Account credit is invisible and the Next charge amount is wrong
blockers.detail: Repro: on a paid plan remove 3 seats. The dialog says 'You get $69.59 credit on your next bill.' After that the word credit appears nowhere in the portal. Billing home says 'Next charge Dec 23, 2026. $372.00 to your Visa'. Then use 'Make the next payment fail', 'Skip ahead 30 days', 'Run renewals now': the gateway tried $325.61, not $372.00. Adding Pulse (which costs more) showed 'Due today $0.00. Nothing to pay now.' with no reason. The invite seat prompt showed 'Add 1 seat for $23.20 more per month. You pay $0.00 today.' with no reason. Great: billing home shows 'Credit: $46.39. It comes off your next bill.' Next charge reads '$325.61 on Dec 23, after $46.39 credit'. The confirm dialog and the seat prompt show the days left amount, then 'Paid from your credit', then due today. The cancel page says what happens to unused credit. Activity logs the credit. Slack shows its credit balance; we must too.
blockers.where: /billing overview cards, /billing/plan confirm dialog, seat prompt on /settings/organization, /billing/cancel, billing subscription snapshot (credit balance and upcoming invoice amount)

blockers.title: The 'Pick a plan' banner leads to a page where you cannot pick a plan
blockers.detail: Repro: during a free trial with no card, click 'Pick a plan' in the trial banner. It opens /billing/plan titled 'Change your trial apps'. The one filled button is 'Save my apps' and it is greyed out with 'These are the apps in your trial now.' The paying action is the outlined 'Add a card'. Billing home also shows three 'Add a card' buttons in one row next to the banner's 'Pick a plan', and the review screen still shows the 'Pick a plan' banner above it. Three names for one action. Great: one name for the paying action everywhere. The banner goes to the review screen, or to the picker with 'Continue to review' as the single filled button. One filled button per screen. Hide the banner button on the checkout screens.
blockers.where: PlanBanner action target for trial kinds, /billing/plan in trial_change mode, /billing overview cards, /billing/checkout

blockers.title: Every start button on the marketing home page goes down the long road
blockers.detail: All ten start buttons on the home page and the header ('Set up your Stak', 'Start with the WMS' and so on) go to /get-started, a 5 step wizard. Then come name, email and company, a password screen, the picker, the code and the welcome screen: about 10 screens and 12 clicks, and the site itself says 'About five minutes'. The 4 field fast path exists only on /pricing. The research file calls this length the most complained about pattern (HubSpot). Great: header and hero button read 'Start free' and open portal /signup directly (4 fields, 5 clicks). 'Help me choose' stays as the second link to the wizard.
blockers.where: apps/web header, home page hero and footer CTAs, ROUTES and LINKS for the primary CTA

blockers.title: A typo in the email forces the buyer to start over
blockers.detail: On /verify-email the only help is 'Not your address? Sign out and start again.' By then the account, the organization and the one free trial are tied to the wrong address, and the company name is used. Great: a 'Change email' link on this screen. One field, save, a new code goes out to the new address, and the organization and the trial stay. Rate limited and only allowed while the email is unverified.
blockers.where: apps/portal /verify-email, auth server action for changing an unverified email

blockers.title: Password hint names one rule, the form enforces four
blockers.detail: The hint under the field reads 'At least 10 characters.' A 28 character passphrase ('correct horse battery staple') is refused with 'Include a capital letter.' The other rules (number, capital and small letter, symbol) only show after typing starts, and errors arrive one at a time. Linear, Slack and Notion need no password at all. Great: state every rule before the first key press and show all unmet rules at once, or accept any long passphrase. Best: offer 'Email me a code' so no password is needed.
blockers.where: apps/portal /signup, /reset-password, /invite password field hint and validation copy; packages/auth password policy

blockers.title: Setup guide promises 5 steps, then shows 8, then 12
blockers.detail: The last welcome step said 5 steps and 'about 12 min in all'. The launcher then said '1 of 8 complete, about 15 min left'. After adding Pulse it said '2 of 12 complete, about 19 min left', and the same long list sits on the Organization settings page. SPEC 5.7 says 3 to 5 steps. Also, a wizard buyer who skips 'Looks good' sees step 1 'Tell us about your business' as not done even though they answered on the site. Great: the launcher shows the same 5 steps and minutes the welcome screen promised, with 'Show more steps' for the rest, and counts wizard answers as done.
blockers.where: apps/portal launcher setup guide, /welcome plan step, /settings/organization, setup model

blockers.title: Invoice page does not match the picker and does not add up
blockers.detail: On /billing/invoices/<id> for TEST-0001: 'Promo code TEST10 (10% off)' is a table line and then appears again as 'Discount'. The three lines sum to $355.68 but 'Subtotal' says $395.20. CRM shows '5 at $23.20' with no word that this is $29 less the 20% bundle discount that the picker shows as its own dollar line. There is no seller name or address and no place where the buyer's address or tax ID prints. The test PDF is plain text with no logo. Great: the invoice repeats the picker lines ('CRM: 5 users x $29 = $145', 'Bundle discount (20%) -$98.80'), lists the promo once, has a subtotal equal to the lines above it, then tax, total and paid. Seller and buyer blocks with address and tax ID. The test PDF uses the email header.
blockers.where: apps/portal /billing/invoices/[id] page, test gateway PDF renderer, invoice line mapping

blockers.title: No trust signals or refund rule on the way in
blockers.detail: Signup and pricing carry no security line and no word on who handles payments until FAQ question 11. No refund answer exists anywhere (a search of apps/web, apps/portal and packages/billing finds none), which matters most for a $4,031 yearly plan. Terms and Privacy are about 300 words each and open inside the CRM app at the CRM origin with CRM navigation. Billing pages have no support contact. Great, with nothing invented: a quiet line under 'Create account' such as 'Card payments run on Stripe. We never see your card number.' One FAQ answer and one line on the cancel page stating the refund rule. Terms and Privacy served from the marketing site with a billing section (renewal, cancel, refund, tax). A support address on billing home. Real customer proof when the owner has it.
blockers.where: apps/portal /signup, apps/web /pricing FAQ (pricing-content.ts), legal link targets, /billing overview, /billing/cancel

blockers.title: Real Stripe has never been run end to end
blockers.detail: Every payment in this review and in the e2e suite used the test gateway and fake clients. The owner decision says payments run on real Stripe. Hosted Checkout, wallets, the Billing Portal, live signed webhooks, Stripe's invoice PDF and how the invoice page maps Stripe's lines are all unseen, so 'production ready' is unproven. Great: one recorded run in Stripe test mode. 'stripe:setup check' prints all ok. Checkout with the working card, a declined card and a bank approval card. A promo code. A card update in the Billing Portal. A replayed webhook. For three carts the Stripe total equals our quote to the cent. This needs test keys from the owner; if none can be had, say so in GO-LIVE.md as the first open item.
blockers.where: packages/billing Stripe adapter and stripe:setup, apps/portal /api/billing/webhooks/stripe, docs/billing/TESTING.md

blockers.title: Small untrue or unclear lines that add up
blockers.detail: 1. Billing home in a trial with no card says 'Your first one arrives when your trial ends.' No invoice arrives without a card; say 'with your first payment'. 2. The email sent when a pause is only planned has the subject 'Your KitStak plan is paused'; it should give the date it will pause. 3. Billing activity listed 'Riley Carter started checkout for CRM and WMS.' four times in a row and logged 1 email of the 6 sent; log each checkout once and log receipts. 4. With Pulse on and 8 people the picker says 'talk to us' and lets you go on without saying which 5 people get Pulse. 5. The confirm dialog for a paid change does not name the card that will be charged.
blockers.where: /billing overview invoices empty state, packages/billing emails (paused template), /billing/activity audit writes, PlanPicker Pulse note, plan change confirm dialog
